texts.preamble: Velankanni vs The Secretary To Government on 28 December, 2017 Author: M.S.Ramesh Bench: M.S.Ramesh, G.R.Swaminathan In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 28.12.2017 Coram The Hon'Ble Mr.Justice M.S.Ramesh And The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice G.R.Swaminathan W.P.No.34081 of 2017 and WMP.No.37826 of 2017 Velankanni .. Petitioner Vs. 1 The Secretary to Government, Municipal Administration and Water Supply (M.C.1) Department, Government of Tamil Nadu, Fort St. George, Chennai-9. 2. The Commissioner, Chandavelur Panchayat, Sunguvarchatram 602 106, Sriperambudur Panchayat Union, Kanchipuram District. .. Respondents Prayer: Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of a For Petitioner : Mr.L.Chandrakumar For 1st respondent : Mr.B.Navaneethan Order
texts.facts: 2. The petitioner, who is a differently abled person and running a Bunk Shop opposite to Samsung India Electronics Private Limited, Plot No.D-1, SIPCOT Industrial Part, Phase-II, Walajah Road, Sunguvarchatram 602 106, Sriperambudur Taluk, Kanchipuram District, apprehends that the Velankanni vs The Secretary To Government on 28 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109119210/ 1 respondents evict him from that place. In this regard, the petitioner has given a representation dated 10.11.2017 to the respondents. Since, the same has not been disposed of by the respondents, the petitioner has approached this Court by way of filing the present Writ Petition. 3. In an identical situation, a Division Bench of this Court in W.P.No.27049/2017 dated 23.10.2017 has held as follows in paragraphs Nos.2 to 6 : ''2. The petitioner claims that he is a differently-abled person having Locomotor Disability of 80% and he is running a Bunk shop at Haddows Road, Opposite to Standard Chartered Bank, Nungambakkam, Chennai 600 034, and he claims that he is selling tea, coffee and food items in an hygienic manner by using LPG stove and out of the meager income earned, he is maintaining himself as well as his family.
texts.arguments: The petitioner would further state that he is entitled to the benefits of the benevolent Central Legislation, viz., the Street Vendors [Protection of Livelihood] Act, 2014 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder and till the formalities contemplated under the Act are fully complied with, the petitioner cannot be evicted from the present place of business and the petitioner, in this regard, has submitted a representation dated 04.10.2017 to the respondents seeking for permission / licence to continue to run the Bunk shop in the said place and apprehending dispossession, he came forward to file the present writ petition. 3 Mr.L.Chandrakumar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner on instructions, would submit that the petitioner is running the Bunk shop in the above said address for very many years and that, he has not sub-let or part with the interest or possession of the Bunk shop in question and he continues to run the same and selling the food articles prepared in an hygienic manner and is strictly complying with the relevant Food Safety Norms and Rules and unless and until the identification and enumeration process is done as per the provisions of the above said Act, the petitioner may not be disturbed from the Bunk Shop in question and would further submit that the petitioner had submitted a representation to the Town Vending Committee/2nd respondent herein and hence, prays for appropriate orders. 4 Per contra, Mr.A.Nagarajan, learned Standing counsel appearing for the respondents would submit that immediate, urgent and necessary steps have already been taken to form the Town Vending Committee and enumeration process is going on and it is for the petitioner to substantiate his plea that he is running the Bunk shop in question for very many years without parting with either the possession or interest or both in respect of the said bunk shop. 5
